explanation.surface: A popular figure is too ungrateful to thank a skeleton crew on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Sought-after suggests a celebrity; the ungrateful person and the cut staff are the two sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanted by many people at once, much requested.

clue.text: Protected dummies in crashes

indicators.note: a crash smashes things apart, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Crash-test dummies are shielded when the car hits the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Crashes sounds like the test, but it is the instruction that smashes the letters of dummies in.
explanation.definitionFit: Given immunity by vaccination, so shielded against a disease.

clue.text: Dog Tycho Brahe?

definitions.meaning: a very large breed of dog
the 16th-century Danish astronomer, a famous man from Denmark

explanation.surface: Who was Tycho Brahe? A dog?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: the astronomer was a notable Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed name, and a fair description of the eminent Danish astronomer.

clue.text: Terribly angered

indicators.note: letters treated terribly are knocked out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who is extremely cross.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the anagram of angered, and a straight description of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Being furious means being made very cross, which is the whole clue read plainly.

clue.text: Right to replace first portion of peculiar liquid

indicators.note: the first portion of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: funny = odd, peculiar
R = right
the opening letter, which R replaces

explanation.surface: A right to swap the first part of an odd liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: Peculiar suggests a strange liquid, but it is the word FUNNY, which loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: A runny sauce or egg flows easily, it is fluid.
